PullRequest.Title: Agents window: pin custom session groups
PullRequest.Body:

Adds pinning for whole custom session groups in the Agents window sessions list.

## Changes

- **Pin Group / Unpin Group** on the header toolbar and context menu of top-level custom groups (not nested groups or comparisons). The pinned flag is stored with the group in `ISessionGroupsService` profile storage, survives delete/undo, and is cleared when the group is nested in another group.
- **Placement:** outside Inbox, a pinned group renders inside the Pinned section, after the pinned sessions, in its user-managed order. Pinned is shown while it holds a pinned group. Unpinning returns the group to its place in the top-level order.
- **Pinned header:** its status icon, count and accessible label include the sessions of its pinned groups (new optional `ISessionSection.subtreeSessions`), corrected after comparisons are attached to their originating sessions, including participants that "Show less" hides.
- **First pin:** pinning the first group expands Pinned, like pinning the first session, unless the user chose Pinned's collapse state.
- **Drag and drop:** pinned groups reorder only among themselves. Another header dropped among them lands first below them, before the first unpinned header in the order, so a nested group can always return to the top level. The insertion line is drawn where the header lands.
- **Menus and tools:** Add to Group / Move to Group list pinned groups first. The `organizeSessionsList` tool infers only custom groups as a header's parent, so a sibling-only `moveHeader` reorders pinned groups.
- `SESSIONS_LIST.md` documents the behavior.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, right-click a top-level custom group and choose **Pin Group**: it moves inside Pinned, which expands.
2. Pin a second group and drag the two to reorder them; drag an unpinned header onto a pinned group and check it lands just below Pinned.
3. Collapse Pinned while a session in a pinned group is unread or needs input: the Pinned header shows the indicator.
4. Choose **Unpin Group**: the group returns to its previous position.
5. Drag a pinned group into another group: it is nested and no longer pinned.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListTools.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionGroupsService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentsWindowRegistrations.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListContextMenu.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chatView/chatViewSessionsList.contribution.test.ts`: passed (793 tests)
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed
- Each new regression test was checked to fail with its fix reverted.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added search-and-drag test at sessionsList.test.ts:9058 demonstrates this reachable state: only Pinned has rows, while other headers retain their nodes. The drag-over call chain and nested scans are explicit; render-count lookups also resolve locations through a sibling indexOf. Magnitude is inferred statically, not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread root-node scans, sibling-array indexOf comparisons, and temporary tree-location arrays
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With H unpinned root headers hidden by search, the loop performs O(H^2) root visits per drag-over. Each accumulated getListRenderCount resolves the root's location using parent.children.indexOf, producing O(H^3) sibling comparisons in this worst case. Search bypasses workspace/worktree section capping, so H includes all distinct unpinned sections after grouping, plus custom groups; repeated drag events repeat the work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread CPU and allocation pressure delays insertion feedback and makes dragging janky in large filtered session lists.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Header-edge drops used the hovered target's supplied index and, for an after-drop, one render-count lookup. The unchanged placement validation could traverse group state, but it did not scan all root nodes separately for every hidden candidate.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new belowPinned feedback path iterates candidate header IDs and calls getTopLevelHeaderIndex for each one. That helper restarts at the root's first child, including search-hidden nodes, and computes preceding render counts on every restart.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 8761 invokes getTopLevelHeaderIndex inside the added _topLevelOrder loop at 8760. Added lines 8783-8789 restart the root traversal and call getListRenderCount for preceding children. Added line 4309 invokes this path from resolveHeaderDrop, which onDragOver calls on every event.
Findings.Title: Avoid rescanning the tree for each hidden drop anchor
Findings.Impact: When a user searches a large worktree/group list so only a pinned subtree matches, then drags a nested header to the top edge of a pinned group to extract it, every drag-over repeats these scans across the hidden headers. Accumulated distinct worktrees can make this expensive even though only a few rows are visible.
Findings.Evidence: SessionsListDragAndDrop.onDragOver calls resolveDrop and resolveHeaderDrop; the new belowPinned branch at 4309 calls getBelowPinnedDropFeedback. With no visible unpinned anchor, 8760-8765 exhaust every candidate and 8783-8789 repeatedly traverse increasingly long root prefixes. objectTreeModel.ts:235-237 and 305-316 resolve each render-count location through indexTreeModel.ts:747-756, whose parent.children.indexOf is linear. listView.ts:1428 calls the delegate before its unchanged-feedback shortcut at 1457, so that shortcut does not coalesce this computation. sessionsList.ts:6427 disables section partitioning during search; groupByWorktree groups by distinct working-directory keys rather than bounding their number.
Findings.Recommendation: Build the current visible-header/index lookup once per feedback calculation, or find the first eligible visible anchor with one tree traversal, instead of restarting the root scan for every candidate. Reuse cumulative row counts within that traversal and preserve the hidden-anchor and leading-section fallback semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial session-list rendering, restored pinned groups, and subsequent session/comparison updates outside Inbox
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The synchronous update builds group items, the Pinned summary, comparison attachments, and tree children before rows can render. Inbox bypasses pinned-group placement. The comparison-summary correction runs before tree.setChildren.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the profile storage cache, then read the existing serialized group-state key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing profile initialization reads the storage collection once; loading pinned flags adds no per-group IPC or filesystem reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same profile storage initialization and group-state read already occurred; the new flag is carried in the existing serialized objects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Storage initialization is an existing startup prerequisite. SessionGroupsService.load subsequently reads cached data synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconcile virtualized tree rows and header status/count rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing groups render once, now inside Pinned rather than at the root. At most one additional Pinned header is created when there were no individually pinned sessions. Summary construction copies the direct pinned sessions and pinned-group subtree sessions; attachment correction traverses the constructed pinned subtree once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The tree already constructed and rendered these custom groups and comparisons. Their placement changes, and the new aggregate summary is linear in its membership rather than duplicating group rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous UI work before the new tree can be displayed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Known sessions S, group hierarchy G, pinned subtree membership P, and attached comparison participants. Capping limits session rows but not the summary's required membership.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous main-thread tree construction. Existing metadata-only session changes schedule a list update; additions/removals remain synchronous. No new concurrent external requests are launched by the changed placement/summary code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Profile state is cached. Existing search matches cache both hits and misses until query/text invalidation. Each update replaces the new pinned-section/id sets and summary arrays; removal/unpinning does not accumulate historical entries. Existing rendering and status subscriptions retain their normal template disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the placement, summary construction, attachment correction, and bounded lifecycle from the complete changed hunks and surrounding update/render code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling measurements; large pinned subtrees increase summary cost, but the inspected change does not establish an avoidable scaling defect in this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence regression: groups are not rendered twice, summary work is bounded and linear, and richer header membership alone does not establish new boundary fan-out or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pin/unpin a group, nest it, delete/undo it, and persist the user's collapse choice
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command mutates group state, synchronously serializes the existing state key, fires group-change listeners, and refreshes the visible list. First pin may also save Pinned's collapse state. Database persistence is not awaited by the command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize groups, memberships, child orders, and appearances into the existing profile-state key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One save per effective pin/unpin mutation; unchanged pin values and nested-group pin attempts return without saving. No per-member pin or provider operation occurs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This pin-group action did not exist. Existing rename/appearance/nesting/deletion actions already saved the same complete state through this helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: JSON serialization remains synchronous on the action path; actual storage flushing is deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush pending profile-key changes to the storage process/database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Pending inserts are keyed and coalesced by the existing throttled delayer. Group state uses one key; first-pin collapse state can add another key to the same flush, not one request per group member.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing group mutations used the same cached/coalesced storage path. The new action adds bounded key updates, not a new persistence mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate UI action's critical path; commands do not await storage flush.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Serialized group/membership state size and number of effective user mutations, not the number of sessions as independently pinned operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous mutation/listeners; deferred storage flushes use the existing throttled delayer. No subprocess, session-provider IPC, or network call is made to pin a group.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged values are no-ops. Profile gets read the storage cache; identical storage strings are suppressed. Pending writes coalesce per key. New pinned-id sets are replaced and bounded by current groups; delete/undo preserves only the requested existing group snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from mutation guards, save, storage cache/flush implementation, and group-change listeners.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: State serialization and the new group scan can cost more for very large profiles, but action frequency and actual durations are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new action follows existing mutation/persistence ownership and does not fan out into per-session work. The extra group scan on change is bounded; no leak or uncontrolled background resource creation was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extract a nested header by dragging over a pinned group while find hides the unpinned headers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every drag-over synchronously resolves placement and below-Pinned insertion feedback before returning to the list's drag handler. The existing unchanged-feedback shortcut runs only after this computation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist changed group parent/order after an actual drop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero storage or provider calls during hover. Actual drop uses bounded existing group/order key mutations, coalesced by storage; it does not move or archive each session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Header drops already persisted parent/order changes through these helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the actual drop mutates/serializes state; storage IPC is deferred. The reported hover slowdown is local CPU work, not boundary latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H distinct unpinned top-level headers after grouping plus custom groups, and repeated drag-over events. In Worktree grouping, each distinct working directory contributes a section. Find disables section partitioning, retains nonmatching root nodes, and can leave only the pinned subtree visible.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely serialized on the main UI thread. Each drag-over invokes the resolver even when the target and feedback are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cached header-index table or repeated-target coalescing exists before the new scan. Search's hit/miss cache does not remove hidden tree nodes. Render-node counts are stored, but public getListRenderCount resolves each node location through a linear sibling indexOf. Warm search/unchanged insertion feedback therefore does not eliminate the CPU work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: complete call chain, list handler ordering, root scans, location lookup, search partitioning, and an added test demonstrating the only-Pinned-visible extraction scenario were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured drag latency. Large accumulated worktree/group collections are the scaling trigger; prevalence and exact duration affect severity, not the proven mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one introduced medium-severity repeated-work regression at sessionsList.ts:8761: exhausting H hidden candidates restarts root scans, giving O(H^2) root visits and O(H^3) worst-case sibling comparisons through render-count location lookup. Previously insertion feedback used the supplied target index and at most one render-count lookup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Add/Move to Group menus and use readSessionsList / organizeSessionsList to reorder pinned sibling headers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menus build the group display order locally. Tools build/read snapshots, infer a custom-group parent, apply operations in order, and serialize their result before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and serialize the existing session-tree/tool-result representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot per requested read or sibling-parent inference, with existing pre-consumer updates between stale operations. Pinned placement adds a container header, not repeated copies of every session tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Tools already constructed snapshots, recursively searched them, and serialized results. The changed parent inference ignores presentation sections; traversal frequency is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot construction/result serialization are on the tool response path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist header reordering through existing storage helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded state-key mutations per operation, coalesced by storage. Opening menus or reading a snapshot does not issue provider/network calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Programmatic header organization already used these mutation and storage paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local mutations/update precede the tool response; database flush is deferred.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current groups and descendants for menu order; snapshot session/header nodes and number of tool operations for organization. The new pinned-first partition processes top-level groups, not session contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local synchronous traversal. Tool operations are applied sequentially with awaited operation completion and updates before subsequent state-reading operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pinned-first order is constructed on demand. Existing snapshot and comparison/group lookups remain authoritative; no new persistent cache or retained historical state is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed recursive call, tool operation loop, getGroupsInDisplayOrder, and moveHeaderTo.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large snapshots have existing serialization cost; no new multiplicative cost or measured increase was established here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: changed parent semantics do not increase snapshot frequency or external calls, and menu partitioning does not establish a new hot collection-wide mechanism beyond existing group enumeration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark all sessions in Pinned as done/archive them, including pinned groups, then undo
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Confirmation precedes the existing archive batch. Active-chat cancellation completes before provider archive batches. The notification waits for batch settlement. Undo restores archived candidates sequentially; remote lifecycle operations can remain on that action path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load active chat models and cancel active requests through the existing chat service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Calls are controlled by active chats, not all history entries: idle sessions skip cancellation loads. Up to four sessions cancel concurrently, with a session's active chats processed sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pinned's bulk action used only its direct sessions. The diff intentionally includes pinned-group subtrees using the same cancellation path already used by group bulk actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All cancellations settle before archive provider batches start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire session subscriptions, initialize cold state when needed, and dispatch/await confirmed archive actions across the agent-host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Management groups candidates by provider and invokes one archiveSessions batch per capable provider. Agent-host batches use a provider-wide limiter of four, then issue an archive operation per eligible session. Existing live subscriptions are shared by URI; cold unheld session URIs require a snapshot, not one snapshot per history item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped batching, shared subscriptions, and four-operation limiter served direct pinned sessions and existing group archive actions. The diff expands the user-selected scope without changing per-session protocol frequency or concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold subscription initialization and action acknowledgement are awaited before an archive settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect an unavailable dev-container host when needed and stop the container after its last unarchived session is archived.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Archive/unarchive are serialized per session; dev-container archive/lifecycle work is additionally limited to one operation per provider. Successful stop is guarded by the remaining unarchived-session check, not performed independently for every session in a batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing archive actions already reached this lifecycle logic. Including pinned-group members can now reach it from the Pinned section, with unchanged serialization and stop guards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Lifecycle confirmation/stop can delay completion of a dev-container archive. An already connected host bypasses reconnect.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update detached-worktree archive state through the source agent-host service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only sessions carrying detached-worktree handles make this call. Existing connection/lifecycle ownership and failure rollback remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same calls occurred when these sessions were archived individually or through their custom group. The Pinned section now intentionally includes them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited as part of remote archive/unarchive completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K unarchived candidates from direct pinned sessions plus pinned-group subtrees, provider groups, distinct subscription URIs, and active chats. Direct pinned-session precedence excludes those sessions from regular group-member arrays; attached comparison correction uses a session-id map.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation limited to four sessions for the batch. Management groups provider calls; fallback single-session archives use the same limiter. Agent-host archiveSessions has a provider-wide limiter of four across batches. Remote actions serialize per session, dev-container archives serialize per provider, and undo restores sessions sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Idle-session cancellation skips loads. Agent-host subscriptions coalesce by URI; existing healthy entries are shared, errored entries are evicted on reacquisition, and references are disposed after confirmation. Provider metadata caches and already-connected dev-container fast paths are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the expanded target set and inspected cancellation/provider/protocol/lifecycle call paths. Detailed chat-model loading internals and backend durations were not fully established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold model/history size, transport latency, and container reconnect/stop duration are unmeasured. These affect action latency but do not establish an avoidable diff-introduced scheduling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: expanded target membership is required bulk-action behavior, while existing provider grouping, global-per-provider limits, subscription ownership, and archive-change batching are preserved. The diff does not replace a batch with unbounded per-session concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base f9888d5ae288daf7a461d46907453bec764ec33c and head 4075a8cc7c0ad614db5615dc3a4a2a6ddf4fa56a. Inspected the full 10-file inventory and all diff pages, surrounding rendering/search/DnD/storage/tool code, and bulk archive provider/protocol concurrency. Submitted one high-confidence introduced drag-feedback CPU finding. No concrete performance-regression fix requiring blame provenance was identified. Static review only; no timings or benchmark results are claimed.
